segments.text: Japan news in eighty seconds. Here are three updates, checked on October second.
First, Japan has begun recovering a Global Hawk surveillance drone from the sea off Tottori.
Associated Press reports that it disappeared in mid September.
What may be its main body was located about two hundred to three hundred meters underwater.
Second, Economy Minister Minoru Kiuchi says Japan no longer needs excessively loose monetary policy now that it has moved beyond deflation.
Reuters reports he stressed that interest rate decisions belong to the Bank of Japan.
He declined to say whether the government opposed additional rate increases.
That is a minister's position, not a new central bank rate decision.
In its October first Tankan release, the Bank of Japan reported large manufacturers at plus twenty four, up from plus twenty two in June.
Large nonmanufacturers slipped from plus thirty seven to plus thirty five.
These are sentiment index readings, not growth rates.
The survey measures favorable responses minus unfavorable responses.
Sources: Associated Press, Reuters, and the Bank of Japan.
